summary: Log lookout built around 1904 by the Mount Pleasant Hotel Company, replaced by a steel tower on Mount Hale in 1929; guy wires and roof remnants remain.

facts.design: Log structure, probably about 20 feet tall, guy wired to boulders
facts.status_note: The structure is gone. The Forest Fire Lookout Association lists it as gone, and NH Family Hikes files Mt. Rosebrook under mountains which once had a fire tower. White Mountain History describes guy wires and roof remnants at the site.

staffing.status: On duty during times of need, with a telephone line to the hotel

events.note: Built by the Mount Pleasant Hotel Company, around 1904 according to White Mountain History; NH Family Hikes dates it only to shortly after the fires.
White Mountain History says the steel Mount Hale Lookout Tower replaced the Rosebrook lookout.

evidence.supports: Mount Pleasant Hotel Company built the first lookout in the White Mountains around 1904 on the blackened summit
evidence.quote: The Mount Pleasant Hotel Company built the first lookout in the White Mountains around 1904 on the already blackened summit of Mount Rosebrook.

evidence.supports: Mount Rosebrook is 3,004 feet and in Bethlehem
The log structure probably stood about 20 feet tall
evidence.quote: The log structure overlooked the Zealand Valley and Bretton Woods and probably stood only 20 feet tall.

evidence.supports: The structure was guy wired to boulders
evidence.quote: It was guy wired to boulders to keep it from blowing over.

evidence.supports: A telephone line linked the lookout to the hotel; it was on duty in times of need
evidence.quote: A telephone line provided communications to the hotel and the lookout was on duty during times of need.

evidence.supports: NH Family Hikes calls it a fire tower built shortly after the fires
evidence.quote: Shortly after this disaster, the Mt. Pleasant Hotel Company built a fire tower on Mt. Rosebrook, which had already been burned in the fires.

evidence.supports: A steel tower on Mount Hale replaced the Rosebrook lookout in 1929
evidence.quote: The Rosebrook Lookout was replaced in 1929 by the steel Mount Hale Lookout Tower

evidence.supports: Remains today are guy wires and the roof remains
evidence.quote: Little remains of the Mount Rosebrook Fire Tower today other than guy wires and the remains of the roof that is covered with leaves and spruce needles.

evidence.supports: Forest Fire Lookout Association lists Rosebrook as gone, type unknown
NH Family Hikes lists Mount Rosebrook among mountains which once had a fire tower
evidence.quote: Mountains which Once Had a Fire Tower

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NH Family Hikes calls the 1904 lookout a fire tower; White Mountain History describes a log structure in detail. The story follows White Mountain History.

notes_for_editor: Built date and design follow White Mountain History; NH Family Hikes gives only 'shortly after the fires' and calls it a fire tower. NH Family Hikes files Mt. Rosebrook under 'Mountains which Once Had a Fire Tower' (an earlier draft said it was under 'Active Fire Towers'; that was a misreading and is corrected here). That heading agrees with the FFLOS 'Gone' listing and with White Mountain History. Access to the site today is not stated in any source read. The NHDFL state history PDF (forest-lookout-towers-history.pdf) returned HTTP 403 and was not read. Mt. Hale: FFLOS lists it as Tower Gone, and NH Family Hikes lists Mt. Hale (Bethlehem) under 'Mountains which Once Had a Fire Tower' too, not among active towers as an earlier note said. The Seacoast Online 2017 article, seen only as a search snippet, was not used.
